When some test files are named `user.test.ts` and others `user.spec.ts`, a glob or a search written for one name misses the other.

By default, a file that ends in `.test` or `.spec` plus `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts` or `.tsx` is a test file, and it must use `.test`. Only the file's path counts, not what's in the file.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"vitest/consistent-test-filename" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default. The ones that are commented out are unset by default.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"vitest/consistent-test-filename" = ["error", {
  # pattern = <value>,
  # allTestPattern = <value>,
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"filename": "src/user.spec.ts"} */}
```ts src/user.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("has a name", () => {
  expect(loadUser().name).toBe("Ada");
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good {"filename": "src/user.test.ts"} */}
```ts src/user.test.ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("has a name", () => {
  expect(loadUser().name).toBe("Ada");
});
```

## Options

Both options are regular expressions, written as strings and tested against the file's path. `/pattern/` works too, but flags after the last slash are ignored.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pattern` | `.*\.test\.[tj]sx?$` | The pattern a test file's path must match. |
| `allTestPattern` | `.*\.(test\|spec)\.[tj]sx?$` | Which files are test files. Other files aren't checked. |

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"vitest/consistent-test-filename" = ["error", { pattern = '.*\.spec\.ts$' }]
```

With that `pattern`, `.test.ts` is the name that gets reported:

{/* bad {"options": [{"pattern": ".*\\.spec\\.ts$"}], "filename": "src/user.test.ts"} */}
```ts src/user.test.ts
import { test } from "vitest";

test.todo("has a name");
```

With `allTestPattern` set to `__tests__`, every file with `__tests__` in its path is a test file. This one is reported because it doesn't end in `.test.ts`:

{/* bad {"options": [{"allTestPattern": "__tests__"}], "filename": "__tests__/user.ts"} */}
```ts __tests__/user.ts
import { test } from "vitest";

test.todo("has a name");
```
